Q: How to fix mutable objects inside a copy of IReadOnly copy of a list A:

IReadOnlyList<T> only makes the collection read-only (no Add/Remove). It does not make the items immutable, and there’s no way for it to “protect you” from someone mutating the objects inside, that’s by design.
The real problem you’re describing is usually modifying the world membership while you’re iterating (Instantiate/Delete during UpdateAll / DrawAll). The standard fix is to stop exposing the live list and buffer adds/removes (command queue), then apply them at safe points (start/end of update).

Example idea: keep _gameObjects private have _pendingAdd / _pendingRemove, Instantiate() adds to pending list, Delete() adds to pending remove list, Flush() applies changes before/after update loop That way objects can still be mutated normally (you need that), but the collection won’t change while you’re iterating.

Also note: calling _gameObjects.ToList() every frame allocates and hides the real issue. Better to fix it properly with a buffer rather than copying each frame. If you really need external code to iterate safely, return a snapshot of references (_gameObjects.ToArray()), not deep copies, you’ll still mutate the same objects, but membership is stable for that pass.

Q: Can I use angular effects for API calls? A:

Use rxResource, resource, httpResource for API calls, it basically does the same thing and is a dedicated feature for GET API calls.

Yes, resource is experimental, but works great and will become stable in future, plus it makes coding and handling API calls easier.

It can react to the signals, in the same way effect does.

Q: Prometheus cannot scrape kubernetes metrics A:

Prometheus target error:
serviceMonitor/monitoring/kube-prometheus-kube-prome-kube-etcd/0
Error scraping target:Get "http://IP_ADDRESS:2381/metrics": dial tcp IP_ADDRESS:2381: connect

Solution:

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: etcd-proxy-config
  namespace: kube-system
data:
  haproxy.cfg: |
    global
      log stdout format raw local0
    
    defaults
      mode tcp
      timeout connect 5s
      timeout client 30s
      timeout server 30s
      log global

    frontend etcd-external
      bind "${NODE_IP}:2381"
      default_backend etcd-local

    backend etcd-local
      server etcd-1 127.0.0.1:2381

---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: etcd-proxy
  namespace: kube-system
  labels:
    app: etcd-proxy
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: etcd-proxy
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: etcd-proxy
    spec:
      hostNetwork: true
      nodeSelector:
        node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane: ""
      tolerations:
      - key: "node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane"
        operator: "Exists"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
      - key: "node-role.kubernetes.io/master"
        operator: "Exists"
        effect: "NoSchedule"
      containers:
      - name: haproxy
        image: haproxy:3.3.0-alpine
        args: ["-f", "/usr/local/etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg"]
        env:
        - name: NODE_IP
          valueFrom:
            fieldRef:
              fieldPath: status.hostIP
        volumeMounts:
        - name: config
          mountPath: /usr/local/etc/haproxy/haproxy.cfg
          subPath: haproxy.cfg
        livenessProbe:
          exec:
            command:
            - /bin/sh
            - -c
            - "nc -z 127.0.0.1 2381"
          initialDelaySeconds: 10
          periodSeconds: 10
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 100m
            memory: 128Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 50m
            memory: 64Mi
      volumes:
      - name: config
        configMap:
          name: etcd-proxy-config
